pose.ref.overstride: at most {lim} cm, shin at most {shin}°
pose.finding.cadence.title: Cadence
pose.finding.cadence.ok: Cadence, {value} steps/min, is reasonable for the speed.
pose.finding.cadence.problem: Cadence, {value} steps/min, is low for the speed. Fewer, longer steps often come with overstriding and higher loads on knee and hip. A 5–10 % higher cadence reduces knee and hip loading (Heiderscheit et al. 2011).
pose.finding.cadence.cue: Think “quick, short steps” and let the foot land closer to the body. Increase by 5 % at a time.
pose.finding.cadence.drill: Run 3 × 2 min to a metronome at {target} beats/min, with easy jogging in between.
pose.finding.overstride.title: Overstride
pose.finding.overstride.ok: The foot lands close under the body: heel {value} cm ahead of the hip, shin {shin}° from vertical.
pose.finding.overstride.problem: The heel lands {value} cm ahead of the hip and the shin tilts {shin}° forward at contact. This brakes every step and sends a bigger impact up through shin and knee.
pose.finding.overstride.ok_shin: The shin is close to vertical ({shin}°) at contact.
pose.finding.overstride.problem_shin: The shin tilts {shin}° forward at contact, so the foot lands ahead of the knee. This brakes every step and sends a bigger impact up through shin and knee.
pose.finding.overstride.cue: Land with the foot under the knee – “put the foot down under you” – and let cadence rise a little.
pose.finding.overstride.drill: A-skips and high knees 3 × 20 m, then 3 × 1 min running focused on landing under the knee.
pose.finding.knee_stiff_contact.title: Straight knee at landing
pose.finding.knee_stiff_contact.problem: The knee is almost straight ({value}° flexion) at contact. A slightly bent knee absorbs the impact more softly.
pose.finding.knee_stiff_contact.cue: Land with a soft knee, think of springing into the landing.
pose.finding.knee_stiff_contact.drill: Skipping rope 3 × 30 s with soft, quiet landings.
pose.finding.knee_flex_low.title: Stiff knee in stance
pose.finding.knee_flex_low.problem: The knee bends only {value}° in stance. A stiff leg gives a harder impact and more bounce.
pose.finding.knee_flex_low.cue: Give a little at the knee when the foot lands and let the body sink softly.
pose.finding.knee_flex_low.drill: Single-leg squats 3 × 10 per leg, slow down and controlled up.
pose.finding.knee_flex_high.title: Deep knee bend in stance
pose.finding.knee_flex_high.problem: The knee bends {value}° in stance. This loads the front of the thigh and the kneecap more than needed and costs energy.
pose.finding.knee_flex_high.cue: Run “tall”: long spine and a quick push-off.
pose.finding.knee_flex_high.drill: Pogo jumps 3 × 20 and fast feet 3 × 15 s.
pose.finding.trunk.title: Trunk lean
pose.finding.trunk.ok: The trunk leans {value}° forward, a moderate lean.
pose.finding.trunk_upright.title: Upright trunk
pose.finding.trunk_upright.problem: The trunk leans only {value}° forward. A slight forward lean shifts some load from the knee to the hip and hamstrings (Teng and Powers 2014).
pose.finding.trunk_upright.cue: Lean the whole body slightly forward from the ankles, not from the waist.
pose.finding.trunk_upright.drill: Falling starts: lean forward until you must step, then run 20 m, 5 times.
pose.finding.trunk_forward.title: Strong forward lean
pose.finding.trunk_forward.problem: The trunk leans {value}° forward. That much lean loads the lower back and hip flexors and often shortens the stride.
pose.finding.trunk_forward.cue: Think “tall”: head towards the ceiling, eyes forward.
pose.finding.trunk_forward.drill: Plank and glute bridge 3 × 30 s so the trunk can hold its position.
pose.finding.hip_ext_low.title: Short push-off
pose.finding.hip_ext_low.problem: The thigh reaches only {value}° behind vertical at toe-off. Little hip extension often goes with tight hip flexors or weak glutes.
pose.finding.hip_ext_low.cue: Push off backwards, as if driving the belt back with the foot.
pose.finding.hip_ext_low.drill: Hip flexor stretch 2 × 45 s per side and lunges with knee drive 3 × 10.
pose.finding.vertical_osc.title: Bounce
pose.finding.vertical_osc.ok: The pelvis moves {value} cm up and down per step, a moderate bounce.
pose.finding.vertical_osc.problem: The pelvis moves {value} cm up and down per step. Bounce that does not move you forward costs energy (Folland et al. 2017).
pose.finding.vertical_osc.cue: Think “forward, not up” and shorten the step slightly.
pose.finding.vertical_osc.drill: Run 3 × 1 min looking at a spot on the wall and keep the spot still.
pose.finding.foot_strike.title: Foot strike
pose.finding.foot_strike.heel: Heel strike: the heel touches the belt first (foot {value}° from flat). The most common way to run and not a fault in itself; where the foot lands matters more (Hamill and Gruber 2017).
pose.finding.foot_strike.midfoot: Midfoot strike: the whole foot touches the belt almost at once (foot {value}° from flat).
pose.finding.foot_strike.forefoot: Forefoot strike: the forefoot touches the belt first (foot {value}° from flat). This loads calves and Achilles tendons more; build calf strength if you changed recently.
pose.finding.asymmetry.title: Left–right difference
pose.finding.asymmetry.problem: {metric} differs {value} % between sides: {left} left and {right} right. Some difference is normal; larger ones can come from an old injury, weakness or habit.
pose.finding.asymmetry.cue: Ask about pain or stiffness on that side and follow up at the next test.
pose.finding.asymmetry.drill: Single-leg work (single-leg squats, hops) 3 × 10 per leg, starting with the weaker side.
pose.finding.pelvic_drop.title: Pelvic drop
pose.finding.pelvic_drop.ok: The pelvis stays stable ({value}° at most).
pose.finding.pelvic_drop.problem: The opposite hip drops {value}° when you stand on the {side} leg. This suggests the outside of the hip does not hold, and is more common in runners with knee and hip complaints (Bramah et al. 2018).
pose.finding.pelvic_drop.cue: Think “high hips”, as if a string pulls you up at the navel.
pose.finding.pelvic_drop.drill: Side plank with hip lift 3 × 30 s and banded clamshells 3 × 15 per side.
pose.finding.knee_valgus.title: Knee collapses inwards
pose.finding.knee_valgus.problem: The knee moves {value}° inwards from the hip–foot line when you stand on the {side} leg.
pose.finding.knee_valgus.cue: Keep the knee pointing the same way as the toes when the foot lands.
pose.finding.knee_valgus.drill: Single-leg squats in front of a mirror with a band around the knees, 3 × 10 per leg; keep the knee over the foot.
pose.finding.step_width.title: Feet cross the midline
pose.finding.step_width.problem: The feet land {value} cm apart, almost on one line or crossing. Narrow steps raise the load on the shins (Meardon and Derrick 2014).
pose.finding.step_width.cue: Think of running on two rails, not on a tightrope.
pose.finding.step_width.drill: Run 3 × 1 min along a taped line on the belt with one foot on each side.
pose.finding.arm_cross.title: Arm crosses the midline
pose.finding.arm_cross.problem: The {side} hand crosses the body midline by {value} cm. The arms then twist the upper body instead of balancing the legs.
pose.finding.arm_cross.cue: Let the arms swing forward and back, “pocket to chin”.
pose.finding.arm_cross.drill: Standing arm swings in front of a mirror 3 × 30 s, then 3 × 1 min running with the same movement.
pose.finding.heel_whip.title: Heel whip
pose.finding.heel_whip.problem: The heel swings {value}° {direction} right after toe-off on the {side} foot. This often comes with rotation at the hip or foot.
pose.finding.heel_whip.cue: Think of lifting the foot straight up towards the buttock.
pose.finding.heel_whip.drill: Butt kicks 3 × 20 m on a straight path and single-leg balance 3 × 30 s per leg.
pose.kf.caption.contact: The plumb line runs through the hip. The foot should land close to it, with a slightly bent knee.
pose.kf.caption.midstance: The knee is at its deepest bend and the leg carries the whole body weight.
pose.kf.caption.toe_off: The foot leaves the belt. The hip should be extended, with the thigh behind the plumb line.
pose.kf.caption.flight: No foot on the belt. The dashed line shows the height of the hip.
pose.kf.caption.sequence: One step with the {side} foot: contact, midstance, toe-off and flight.
pose.warn.low_fps: The video has {fps} frames/s. {metrics} are uncertain here and reliable from {need} frames/s.
pose.warn.no_height: Height is missing, so distances in centimetres cannot be calculated.
pose.warn.few_steps: Only {n} steps were found. Record at least 20 seconds of steady running.
pose.warn.low_detection: The runner was found in only {pct} % of the frames. Check the lighting and that the whole body, feet included, is in view.
pose.warn.facing: The runner faces the other way than the chosen camera angle. The analysis follows what the video shows.
pose.warn.scale: Distances in centimetres are estimated from height (about ±{unc} %).
pose.warn.rear_timing: From behind, contact time is less exact than from the side.
pose.error.model_missing: The pose model is missing and could not be downloaded ({reason}). Connect the computer to the internet once, or put the file {name} in the folder {folder}.
pose.error.model_corrupt: The model file {name} is damaged (checksum mismatch).
pose.error.video_open: The video {name} could not be opened.
pose.error.no_runner: No runner was found in the video. Check that the whole body is visible from the side or from behind.
pose.finding.step_width.problem_cross: The feet cross over: each foot lands {value} cm past the midline, as on a tightrope. This raises the load on the shins (Meardon and Derrick 2014).
pose.finding.hip_ext_low.problem_neg: The thigh does not get behind vertical at toe-off ({value}°). Little hip extension often goes with tight hip flexors or weak glutes.
pose.finding.elbow.title: Arm carriage
pose.finding.elbow.problem_straight: The elbow is at {value}° (a straight arm is 180°), and the upper arm swings {swing}° forward and back. Straight arms are heavy and slow and brake the rhythm.
pose.finding.elbow.problem_tight: The elbow is only {value}°, and the upper arm swings {swing}° forward and back. Tightly bent arms give short, stiff arm movements and tense shoulders.
pose.finding.elbow.cue: Keep the elbow around 90° and let the arm swing from the shoulder, relaxed, with the hands between hip and chest.
pose.finding.elbow.drill: Arm swings seated on the floor 3 × 30 s with 90° at the elbow, then 3 × 1 min running with the same movement.
pose.warn.landings_missing: Only {pct} % of the landings could be measured reliably (the foot was hidden or unclear). The values are based on the landings that could be measured.
pose.warn.contact_spread: Contact time varies a lot between steps (half lie between {lo} and {hi} ms). Record again at a higher frame rate or in better light before using the contact time.
pose.warn.contact_implausible: The contact time {ms} ms is outside what is plausible for running ({lo}–{hi} ms). The landings were probably found wrongly, so contact time and the values at landing should not be used.
pose.warn.landings_position: {pct} % of the landings had to be timed from the foot position instead of from when it reaches the belt. Contact time is less certain than usual.
pose.warn.leg_swaps: The program had to correct left and right leg in {pct} % of the frames. Check that both legs are clearly visible and that nothing hides the feet.
pose.warn.fps_hidden: The video has {fps} frames/s, too few for {metrics}. They are not shown: they need {need} frames/s.
